 Okafor makes the difference despite Van Hecke’s defiance – Leeds v Spurs ratings
 Saturday, 7 November 2026, 16:47 
 Photo source: BBC Sport 
 Noah Okafor came off the bench to score a late winner as Leeds United ended Tottenham’s mini-revival at Elland Road. 
 Here are my player ratings for Leeds United and Spurs:
 This is reported by BBC .
 Leeds United
 James Trafford – 6: Alert off his line, with safe handling and a vital late save from Van Hecke. James Justin – 6: Good deliveries and solid defending. Nico Elvedi – 6: Won his physical battle with Marmoush and headed a good chance wide. Tarik Muharemovic – 6: A very solid display. Jayden Bogle – 5: Good going forward, but fortunate not to be sent off for a late challenge on Mathys Tel.
 Advertisement 
 Ethan Ampadu – 7: Leeds’ captain kept the midfield moving and was a strong presence. Sean Longstaff – 6: Booked for a late challenge on Fernandes and had a close-range effort saved. Ao Tanaka – 6: Worked hard but missed a great second-half chance. Gabriel Gudmundsson – 7: Excellent first half with lively runs, before coming off at half-time. Dominic Calvert-Lewin – 6: Worked hard and unselfishly set up a chance Tanaka should have taken. Lukas Nmecha – 5: Struggled and headed straight at Kinsky when he should have scored.
 Melvin Bard – 6: Came on for Gudmundsson at 45 minutes and played some fine forward passes in a decent display. Noah Okafor – 7: Replaced Nmecha at 77 minutes and scored with a clean finish two minutes later; an inspired substitution by Daniel Farke. Harry Wilson – 5: Came on for Tanaka at 77 minutes and tried to create. Unused substitutes: Michael Zetterer, Jaka Bijol, Daniel James and Brenden Aaronson.
 Tottenham
 Antonin Kinsky – 7: Very safe handling and an excellent save from Longstaff. Had no chance with the goal, but had an anxious moment after taking too long over a goal-kick and conceding a corner. Pedro Porro – 6: Willing to join the attack and keen on a tackle; was probably taken off to avoid a red card. Micky van de Ven – 6: A dependable presence in defence, with a vital second-half clearance; booked for hauling back Bogle.
 Jan Paul van Hecke – 7: One of his best games for Spurs, powerful in the air and composed on the ball. Almost saved a point at the end. Andrew Robertson – 6: Solid defensively and energetic in supporting attacks. Archie Gray – 6: Showed some nice touches against his former club but was generally quiet.
 Other news you may find interesting: 
 Leeds United defeated Nottingham Forest 2-0 for a second win in four days, reaching the League Cup third round. Brentford also advanced after beating Birmingham City 6-1. 
 Mykhailo Mudryk has officially joined Tottenham from Chelsea on loan until the end of the 2026/27 season, following a long absence and limited playing time. 
 Vitalii Mykolenko was named player of the match after Everton drew 0-0 with Tottenham, helping the unbeaten Merseyside club remain seventh in the Premier League.
